answer_summary: Macrocycle X is the cyclic oligomer released when the amide-linked (Pinnick-oxidised) Kagome framework COF-7 is degraded by ozonolysis (O3 then Me2S) of the stilbene C=C bonds of its C2 nodes. Its smallest repeat unit is one C2-half plus one D4 residue joined through amide linkages: -NH-C(=O)-C6F4-C(=O)-NH-(1,4-C6H4)-[1,3,5-C6H3(CHO)]-(1,4-C6H4)-, i.e. a 5-formyl-1,3-phenylene bearing two 4-(amide N-H)-phenyl arms alternating with a 2,3,5,6-tetrafluorobenzene-1,4-bis(carbonyl) unit. Repeat-unit formula C27H14F4N2O3; X = cyclo-(C27H14F4N2O3)6 = C162H84F24N12O18 (the ring of 6 C2-halves alternating with 6 D4 units that survives as a closed loop of the Kagome net). Minimality follows from strict alternation of C2-halves and D4 units along the ring (no C2-C2 or D4-D4 adjacency), so no contiguous motif smaller than one C2-half + one D4 can tile the ring.
assumptions: Trusted general chemistry laws: aldimine condensation (aldehyde + primary amine -> imine + H2O, AcOH catalyst); Pinnick-type oxidation of aldimines to amides under NaClO2/NaH2PO4; ozonolysis with reductive (Me2S) work-up cleaving Ar-CH=CH-Ar to two Ar-CHO; inertness of aryl C-F bonds and aromatic rings to all three steps.

Figure-derived inputs read directly from the printed problem: constitution of C2 (stilbene of two 1,3-bis(4-aminophenyl)benzene halves) and D4 (2,3,5,6-tetrafluoroterephthalaldehyde); Kagome topology of COF-7 (pre-printed 'C2 + D4' Kagome entry in the 3.3 table and the printed COF-7 sketch); printed reagent sequence (AcOH, then NaClO2/NaH2PO4, then 1) O3 2) Me2S).

The macrocycle's ring size is taken as the six-repeat closed loop of the Kagome net (6 C2-halves + 6 D4, the 120-degree-wedge pairing that survives C2 node scission); the requested smallest repeat unit (one C2-half + one D4) is independent of this detail.
